panels.title: Bytes by Segment
panels.description: Bytes sent per source segment, across every segment in the data (not filtered by the Segment picker) so it always gives the full picture.

targets.query:
import "regexp"
import "strings"

zone = (ip) =>
  if strings.containsStr(v: ip, substr: ":") then "IPv6"
  else if ip == "0.0.0.0" then "0.0.0.0 unspecified"
 else if ip =~ /^(22[4-9]|23[0-9])\./ then "Multicast"
  else if ip =~ /^255\./ or ip =~ /\.255$/ then "Broadcast"
  else if ip =~ /^169\.254\./ then "Link-local"
  else if ip =~ /^127\./ then "Loopback"
  else if ip =~ /^(10\.|192\.168\.|172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\.)/
    then regexp.replaceAllString(r: /\.[0-9]+$/, v: ip, t: ".0/24")
  else "Public"

from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
  |> group(columns: ["src_ip"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({seg: zone(ip: r.src_ip), _value: r._value}))
  |> group(columns: ["seg"])
  |> sum()

panels.title: Top 10 Talkers — $subnet
panels.description: Repeats once per selected segment. The reverse-DNS target resolves the top-10 IPs of every selected segment at once, so this join is inner (not outer) to keep other segments' hostnames out of this table. First load can be slow with a cold cache: dns-resolver looks IPs up sequentially with a 2s timeout each, then caches. Country is from a local GeoIP database (IP geolocation by DB-IP, db-ip.com); "private network" for any non-public address.

import "regexp"
import "strings"

zone = (ip) =>
  if strings.containsStr(v: ip, substr: ":") then "IPv6"
  else if ip == "0.0.0.0" then "0.0.0.0 unspecified"
  else if ip =~ /^10\.10\./ then " 10.10/16"
  else if ip =~ /^(22[4-9]|23[0-9])\./ then "Multicast"
  else if ip =~ /^255\./ or ip =~ /\.255$/ then "Broadcast"
  else if ip =~ /^169\.254\./ then "Link-local"
  else if ip =~ /^127\./ then "Loopback"
  else if ip =~ /^(10\.|192\.168\.|172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\.)/
    then regexp.replaceAllString(r: /\.[0-9]+$/, v: ip, t: ".0/24")
  else "Public"

from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
  |> group(columns: ["src_ip"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with seg: zone(ip: r.src_ip)}))
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.seg == "$subnet")
  |> sort(columns: ["_value"], desc: true)
  |> limit(n: 10)
  |> rename(columns: {src_ip: "ip", _value: "bytes"})
  |> keep(columns: ["ip", "bytes"])

list.name: site
list.label: Site
list.description: Which tzsp-monitor instance these panels read. Remote sites are the REMOTE_SITE_* lines in properties.yml of the instance serving this Grafana; each is a datasource pointed at that site's own InfluxDB, so nothing is copied between sites. Controls never follow this box: rule suppression and reverse DNS only ever act on the local site, and are inert while another site is selected.

list.name: subnet
list.label: Segment
list.description: Source segments present in the data: named /16 sites, auto-derived /24s for other RFC1918 space, plus Public / Multicast / IPv6 and friends.

import "strings"

zone = (ip) =>
  if strings.containsStr(v: ip, substr: ":") then "IPv6"
  else if ip == "0.0.0.0" then "0.0.0.0 unspecified"
  else if ip =~ /^10\.10\./ then " 10.10/16"
  else if ip =~ /^(22[4-9]|23[0-9])\./ then "Multicast"
  else if ip =~ /^255\./ or ip =~ /\.255$/ then "Broadcast"
  else if ip =~ /^169\.254\./ then "Link-local"
  else if ip =~ /^127\./ then "Loopback"
  else if ip =~ /^(10\.|192\.168\.|172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\.)/
    then regexp.replaceAllString(r: /\.[0-9]+$/, v: ip, t: ".0/24")
  else "Public"

from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
  |> keep(columns: ["src_ip"])
  |> group()

list.name: subnet_talkers
list.label: Segment talkers (internal)
list.description: Hidden helper: top-10 source IPs per selected segment, fed to the reverse-DNS resolver.
list.query:
import "regexp"
import "strings"

zone = (ip) =>
  if strings.containsStr(v: ip, substr: ":") then "IPv6"
  else if ip == "0.0.0.0" then "0.0.0.0 unspecified"
  else if ip =~ /^10\.10\./ then " 10.10/16"
  else if ip =~ /^(22[4-9]|23[0-9])\./ then "Multicast"
  else if ip =~ /^255\./ or ip =~ /\.255$/ then "Broadcast"
  else if ip =~ /^169\.254\./ then "Link-local"
  else if ip =~ /^127\./ then "Loopback"
  else if ip =~ /^(10\.|192\.168\.|172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\.)/
    then regexp.replaceAllString(r: /\.[0-9]+$/, v: ip, t: ".0/24")
  else "Public"

from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
  |> group(columns: ["src_ip"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with seg: zone(ip: r.src_ip)}))
  |> filter(fn: (r) => contains(value: r.seg, set: ${subnet:json}))
